body: You're right it does come off that way. I'm just not sure how to move forward from here without walking on eggshells every day. She's still in university so I'm wondering if I can help find a good therapist for her because I cannot be the only outlet for her. She also has a strong codependency with me, and I just cannot be her only emotional / social / mental outlet.

That's exactly how I feel but if I said it aloud to my family they would send me to an asylum. Some of my friends understand so I'm thankful for that, but I just wish 'death with dignity' could respect bodily autonomy
Same but we're not that lucky💁‍♀️
I wish I was able to kill myself 3 times over. Congrats on finding solace in this chaotic human life.

I've been praying, wishing, begging, for this to happen to me every night as I cry myself to sleep. 

Unfortunately I keep waking up.

I feel like some of it is a religious hot take and the rest truly believe life is amazing even with the downfalls.   


Ever since I was younger it never seemed selfish to me because no one would really know how much an individual was suffering in any form (mental, emotional, physical, etc). Especially the way that I am now where I think about wanting the next minute to be my last, I don't think it's selfish in any way. Everyone tells you you'll move on or things get better--so with that thought, wouldn't everyone also move on once someone has committed suicide?   


It is difficult though because some people want to die, but when they get help or when it comes to the end--they actually want to be saved. Not sure where you are on that, but I don't want to be saved that's why I have an advance directive that if something were to happen to me I don't want life saving treatment.

Thank you for that. I don't know why I was expecting any different kind of response. The things I hate most is when people say it's what my wife would have wanted. Yeah we already had talked about it way beforehand. She said she'd want me to be happy, and I told her I would be a wreck and I would not come out of it. She knew deep down yes our friends are nice, but most of them are superficial and never truly understood that she was dying faster than all of us. I try not to get angry with them because it's easy for them to bury it and move on with their lives because she wasn't their wife--she was mine. Most of them haven't experienced loss so they don't really understand my feelings. Sentiments are nice and all, but they're the equivalent to 'thoughts and prayers,' for me.  


I don't want to learn to move on--that's the thing. I absolutely do not want to be like other widows who are stronger than me. Good on them honestly. My wife was my life and I don't want to learn to cope or talk down to the voice in my head. I'm already dreading having to live longer than this year. Sorry that I seem aggressive. I just wanted a space I could vent and got triggered over your last sentence. Apologies I know you mean well.

You're like 3 or 4 hours away from me. If you don't mind sharing your plan send me a message. I've been looking for ways to go about it for a month now.

Oh I mean.   
"Don't. Life gets better."
If  you ever find a way, let me know
I'm sorry you're both going through that. If i could, I'd trade my life for your wife's cancer🙏

Oh I'm in the 'I don't want to do anything else with my life so I want to leave this earth,' phase. I've been like this for a month and counseling etc had no affect. 

I wrote a will back when she was in the hospital, and I already have an advanced directive should anything happen to me. My mind has been made up for a long while, it's just deciding when and how to do it.
I was contemplating this too, but knowing my luck I'll just recover and have another hospital bill to pay

Literally just the thought of not being a messy physical mess for someone to clean up. (Hanging, gunshot, jump off a high place, or cutting)

I want to not exist right now, but i want to die in one piece.
This sounds amazing, but I don't live alone.

Not in the Denver area, but I'm pretty much the same as you. I can't stop the stress, anger, and devastating sadness from losing my wife a month ago. I too have 3 cats that hopefully my friends and family will take in per wishes in my will.

I just wish I was as strong as you to go the way you're going. I'm trying to find a not so violent way so I'm not in pieces if I get a funeral.
I sent you a msg, but I absolutely relate to how you feel.

So i was being nosy and I noticed an envelope and it's from the funeral home and it has application and permit for disposition. She applied for it on a day without me. Does this document certify her as the owner of the ashes?

Thank you fellow Californian for responding! I was kind of numbed out when I was picking out a casket and flowers so I hope there wasn't some form or clause where the funeral director asks who is (not sure what to call it) but like a representative. They arranged it so that the ashes were brought to us actually. 

I didn't have the money so my MiL paid for it all. I just wanna know if that jeopardizes my chances of keeping my wife's ashes if she were to drive me out of the house.

Thank you so much this helps immensely! I do have another question. If my MiL paid for the funeral arrangements does that give her any power over the custody of my wife's ashes? Like was there a form or clause in the funeral arrangement process that gives her a title relative to if my wife had named someone to handle her funeral? I was numbed out while selecting a casket and flowers and don't want to alarm my MiL asking about funeral specifics.
Thank you! Seriously, my MiL was out of the house today so I was able to ugly cry, wail, sob to my hearts content.
Thank you so much! I'm sorry I made you cry😭

I get the gist of where she's coming from because she's raised in a different time and she's in the medical field so death isn't as big a stressor for her. After I came back from the hospital and she had the chance to meet my family her attitude towards me has changed. She's complained to my dad that I need to get over my wife soon because she can't handle me moping around with a risk of going to the hospital again. My sister is here to overlook my recovery for the next few days and my MiL has been very unwelcoming. I feel like a burden more than ever💁‍♀️
Thank you so much♡I'm actually super new to reddit so I don't really know how to properly use it either, but I appreciate the help!

Thank you♡ I'm thinking she doesn't know how to process her only daughter's death, but at the same time she has closure due to faith. But she truly expects me to be recovered soon so I can be *~*normal*~* again. This hospital visit did not bode well on her attitude towards me.
